name: The Flags Come Down: The End of Empire and the New Nations
description: In thirty years, dozens of colonies became independent states. A story of partition, wars of liberation and the first leaders of new nations.

checkpoints.name: Empires at full stretch
checkpoints.note: By the early 1900s a few European states rule most of Africa and Asia. In India, Indochina and the Dutch East Indies, nationalist movements are already growing under colonial rule.

checkpoints.name: Asia first
checkpoints.note: After the war India, Pakistan, Burma, Sri Lanka, Indonesia and the Philippines become independent, some peacefully and some after fighting. Israel is founded and Vietnam fights France.

checkpoints.name: The African years
checkpoints.note: Seventeen African countries become independent in 1960 alone. Algeria wins after a long war, the Congo falls into crisis soon after independence, and leaders such as Kenyatta and Nyerere take office.

checkpoints.name: The last flags
checkpoints.note: White minority rule in Rhodesia ends in 1980 with Zimbabwe, and South Africa holds free elections in 1994. In 1997 Hong Kong returns to China as the last big British colony.
